evidence: src/business/services/SchedulingService.ts: constructor injects `PatientDao` and `AppointmentDao`, and persistence goes only through calls such as `this.appointments.add`, `this.appointments.setStatus` and `this.patients.get`
src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts: `constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService)` injects the ORM client directly
src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts write(): `this.prisma.visitNote.create({ data: {...} })` is a direct ORM write
src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts notesFor(): `prisma.visitNote.findMany({ where: { appointmentId } })` is a direct ORM query, followed by sorting and mapping in the service
src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts: `export interface VisitNote` is an ad hoc row shape, not a domain entity like the ones SchedulingService uses from ../entities
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit fails because its two files reach persistence in different ways. SchedulingService only goes through the module's persistence ports, AppointmentDao and PatientDao, and turns the raw records into domain entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment). VisitNotesService skips that layer. It takes PrismaService, the ORM client, directly and calls prisma.visitNote.create and prisma.visitNote.findMany itself. It defines its own VisitNote shape instead of a domain entity, and it maps rows by hand. So in one module, one service uses the DAO/repository pattern while the other talks to the ORM directly. The rubric names this as bypassing the module's own abstraction. Both candidate flags check out against the source (lines 13-15 and 21).

The concerns themselves, scheduling and visit notes, both belong to the appointment domain, so they are only loosely cohesive and that is not the main problem. Within SchedulingService, the code that builds an Appointment from a record appears twice (in book and in cancel). That is repeated mapping in one file, not a business rule copied across files, so it is a minor point and not counted as a separate violation.

Confidence is moderate because the source does not show whether a VisitNote DAO exists.

violations.message: VisitNotesService uses the PrismaService ORM client directly (prisma.visitNote.create, prisma.visitNote.findMany) and skips the DAO/port abstraction that the rest of the module uses (SchedulingService goes through AppointmentDao and PatientDao). It also maps rows to its own VisitNote interface instead of a domain entity.
